chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Salim ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Azdi narrated to us from his book in Shawwal in the year 271 AH, saying: Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Tawil narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Sulaym, from Musa ibn Bakr, from al-Fadl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Among matters, there are pending matters, and there are inevitable matters, and the Sufyani is among the inevitable ones that must occur.

key_terms.السُّفْيَانِيَّ: The Sufyani, a key figure in Shia eschatology

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between pending and inevitable events in Shia eschatology according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) categorizes eschatological signs into pending events dependent on human action and inevitable occurrences (muhtamah) determined by divine decree. He specifically identifies the rise of the Sufyani as a guaranteed, inevitable event, underscoring its fixed place in the Shia eschatological timeline. This distinction highlights the balance between divine predestination and human agency in the unfolding of major signs.
